scenes.title: The Crash
scenes.readAloud:
You break the cloud layer and the lush, overgrown jungle of Ajan Kloss rushes up to meet you. The moon is a Green Hell — massive ancient trees, fungal overgrowth, and air so thick with humidity your viewport fogs instantly.

The Ace is flying. Maya is on the secondary stick, eyes on the sensor display.

"Canyon's coming up — bear left two degrees, then drop her like you mean it."

Then the proximity alarm screams. Three contacts on the canyon rim above you — defense turrets, dug into the ridge, tracking you down through the trees. Heavy emplacements. Clone Wars-era hardware that someone has lovingly maintained.

The first burst stitches across the dorsal hull. The cockpit fills with sparks and the shriek of shearing metal. Maya doesn't flinch — she's already throwing power to aft shields.

"They've got us in arc. We can't out-shoot three of those — they're emplacements, they out-mass us. We dive. We get below the canopy line and they lose us. Three rounds — maybe two if you fly clean. Hold her together."

The Banshee is shuddering. The starboard engine is taking hits. The canyon walls are closing in. The turrets keep firing. The only way through is down.

When you finally break below the canopy, the firing stops. The Ace puts the Banshee down hard in a narrow clearing, shearing branches and gouging earth. The ship groans to a stop, listing to port. Smoke curls from the starboard engine cowling.

Maya pops her harness, climbs out of the seat, and assesses. "Good flying. We're alive. Ship's not — yet, but I can fix it. Those turrets, though. Those turrets are going to be a problem on the way out."
scenes.gmNotes:
THE TURRET GAUNTLET: This is a 3-round starship-combat defense-turret gauntlet, NOT a dogfight. Three Clone Wars-era heavy defense turrets (T1, T2, T3) are dug into the canyon rim above the Banshee's approach path. The Banshee is descending into the canyon under fire — the only winning move is to keep diving until they're below the canopy and out of the turrets' fire arc. The party does NOT return fire. The turrets out-mass them and they have nowhere to maneuver to. This is endurance, not combat.

ROUND-BY-ROUND ESCALATION (auto-applied by the Combat Tracker via the encounter's scriptedEscalation field — a banner at the top of the tracker confirms each one):

ROUND 1 — BASELINE: All three turrets attack at their stated ~Power 4 baseline. They roll independently, splitting fire across the Banshee's hull and shields. The Ace (pilot) and Maya (co-pilot) make defensive Piloting + Gunnery checks — primarily managing shield distribution, evasive maneuvers, and absorbing chassis damage. Crew on shields/comms can spend actions to redistribute power, brace for impact, or attempt sensor jamming. Hull/shield damage accumulates. No one fires back.

ROUND 2 — COORDINATED TARGETING: At the top of Round 2 the tracker auto-applies [Optimized] to all three turrets. Their fire-control system has finished triangulating the Banshee's evasion pattern — they're now coordinating their shots. All turret attacks gain +1 Power and the Banshee's defense rolls are stepped down. Damage scales noticeably. Players should feel the squeeze.

ROUND 3 — FOCUS FIRE: At the top of Round 3 the tracker auto-applies [Empowered] on top of [Optimized] to all three turrets. They are now focus-firing on the Banshee's weakest panel — the starboard engine cowling. Hull damage is now severe. The starboard engine begins trailing smoke. The Banshee is one bad roll from a hull breach. END OF ROUND 3: The Banshee drops below the canopy line. Out of arc. Encounter ends.

NO RETURN FIRE: This is non-negotiable. If players insist on firing back from the ventral turret or forward guns, narrate that the angle is wrong (turrets are above and behind), or the trees are blocking line of sight, or the ventral turret can't traverse high enough. The point of this scene is the descent itself — they're trying to survive long enough to get below the canopy. Reward creative defensive thinking (chaff, false transponder, shield rotation tricks) with steps up on the next defensive roll.

SURVIVING THE CRASH: At end of Round 3, the Ace makes ONE final Piloting check (Hard) to put the Banshee on the ground in one piece. Success = clean set-down, ship damaged but flyable after repairs. Failure = harder landing, additional hull damage and minor injuries to one PC, ship still flyable but extra repair time. Either way, they survive. This is the Ace's spotlight — make it earned.

MAYA STAYS BEHIND: After landing, Maya is uninjured but her ship is not. The starboard engine is the worst of it — damaged baffles, coolant leak, cracked manifold. She estimates 12-18 hours for repairs with proper tools. Without a Starship Tool Kit, all repair rolls are stepped down. She gives the heroes TWO objectives:
1. PRIMARY: Find and extract Varth.
2. SECONDARY: Disable the perimeter turret defenses (T1, T2, T3 — the same emplacements that just shot at them). Maya cannot fly extraction past those turrets. "Same three guns that just chewed up my ship are still up on the ridge. If they're live when I lift, I'm dead. Find a way to kill them or I'm flying into a kill box."

This creates a hard permission gate: turrets up = dangerous extraction. Turrets down = clean extraction. The turrets T1/T2/T3 are powered by the fortress generator, which connects directly to the generator sabotage encounter in Mandrake's deal (Adv 1 P2 S5). When the generator blows, T1/T2/T3 go offline and Maya's flight path opens.

IMPORTANT: Maya does NOT accompany the heroes into the jungle or the fortress. She stays with the Banshee. This is both practical (someone needs to fix the ship) and narrative (her conditional extraction is the climax payoff). She is uninjured this time around — the previous V-Wing strafing has been removed. Her staying behind is purely about repairs.

scenes.title: The Green Hell
scenes.readAloud:
The jungle is alive — and hungry. Every step forward is a negotiation with the terrain. Acid pools disguised as standing water hiss when a thrown rock disturbs them. Fungal blooms the size of speeder bikes pulse with a sickly bioluminescence, and you quickly learn that disturbing them triggers a violent detonation of toxic spores.

The canopy closes overhead. The light goes green and strange. Somewhere ahead, through klicks of hostile growth, something waits — and the jungle knows more about you than you know about it.
scenes.gmNotes:
Environmental hazards dominate this scene: Acid Pools (disguised as standing water — hiss when disturbed) and Exploding Fungus Blooms (detonate when touched). Run them as recurring color, not constant rolls — sprinkle them as the crew advances.

GROUP CHALLENGE — "Navigating the Green Hell": This scene is built around a Victory Point (VP) accumulation mechanic. Each PC picks a discipline and describes how they contribute to the trek. The crew is banking VP toward arriving fresh, prepared, and invisible at the fortress perimeter.

MECHANICS:
- Tier 1 / Power 4 across all disciplines
- Each PC rolls Control (stepped down 1 die for T1). Control 4+ = success.
- On success, roll Power vs P4 to determine effect tier:
  • Fleeting (Power loses or ties) = 1 VP
  • Masterful (Power wins) = 2 VP
  • Legendary (Power wins decisively) = 3 VP
  • Mastery (Control 8+) = +1 VP added to the tier result
- 10 VP total = the crew arrives fresh, prepared, and invisible
- Below 10, they arrive in worse condition — injuries, exhaustion, lost gear

FAILURE CONSEQUENCE: A failed Control roll (below 4) means the jungle bites back — acid burns, spore exposure, a predator encounter, or a bad fall. The crew arrives at the fortress perimeter battered. All physical actions in the next scene are stepped down one tier until rest or medical treatment.

VP THRESHOLDS — Read aloud or paraphrase at each threshold:

2 VP: Game trail found threading between fungal blooms — avoids the densest spore zones.

4 VP: Acid pool pattern identified — mineral seeps with discolored soil at the edges. Routable.

6 VP: A sudden absence — the jungle's ambient chatter of insects and calling birds cuts out around the crew for a full thirty seconds, then resumes. Something large and quiet passed nearby and chose not to engage. A PC with the right knowledge skill can identify this as deliberate — not a predator, a person.

8 VP: Sheltered clearing with clean water. Rest stop. Everyone catches their breath.

10 VP: Ghost trek. Every hazard avoided, every predator bypassed. The crew arrives fresh, sharp, and invisible.

SEEDING THE NEXT SCENE: As the crew pushes into the older growth, quietly drop sensory hints that something has been watching them and choosing not to fire — a flicker of movement in the canopy, a single carved bone bead left deliberately on a game-trail rock, footprints that end mid-stride and do not continue. The crew has NOT seen the fortress yet. They do not know where they are on the map. They are about to meet the only person on this moon who does.

SCENE END: When the VP target resolves (success or short), the scene ends with the crew in a pocket of older growth, game trail underfoot, canopy overhead, jungle quiet. No fortress visible. No plan possible yet — they don't know enough. Pause. Let them notice they're being watched. Then cut to Scene 4.

The jungle tests every discipline — acid pools, toxic spores, hostile fauna, and treacherous terrain stand between the crew and the fortress.

thresholds.intel: A faint game trail threads between the worst of the fungal blooms. Following it avoids the densest spore concentrations — someone or something has been using this path regularly.

The acid pools follow a pattern — they cluster around mineral seeps from underground runoff. The discolored soil at their edges is visible once you know what to look for. The crew can route around them.
A ridge line above the canopy offers a clear sightline to the fortress. From here, the crew spots the perimeter layout, the guard towers, and the drainage sluice on the northeast face.

The crew finds a sheltered clearing with clean water — a natural rest point. Ten minutes here and everyone catches their breath. The party arrives at the fortress perimeter rested, hydrated, and sharp.

The Green Hell is behind them. The crew navigated every hazard, avoided every predator, and arrived at the fortress perimeter fresh, prepared, and invisible. No injuries. No lost gear. No alerts. They're ghosts in the jungle.

scenes.title: Ghost in the Canopy
scenes.subtitle: Ajan Kloss — The Ridge
scenes.readAloud:
The trail goes quiet around you. Not the quiet of stillness — the quiet of something deciding. You're catching your breath when a figure drops out of the canopy in front of you. Not a leap. A controlled descent, like he's done it a thousand times.

Lean. Hard. Old Separatist commando gear, patched and rewoven with strips of plant fiber and beadwork that doesn't belong to any culture you recognize. A rifle in his hands, raised, aimed — but his finger is laid alongside the trigger guard, not on the trigger. He's not threatening. He's deciding.

The jungle has gone quiet around him. He's been there the whole time.
scenes.gmNotes:
FIRST CONTACT WITH VAZUS MANDRAKE: A Separatist Holdout Commando, four years past the official surrender order he refused to obey. He didn't keep fighting because he believed in the cause — the cause died and he knows it. He kept fighting because the indigenous Klosari took him in when his unit was dust. He learned their language. He wears their craftsmanship. He is theirs now.

PLAY HIM: Quiet, deliberate, mostly listening. Recurring physical tell — a single carved bone bead that he threads between the fingers of his off hand whenever he's deciding what to say. Use the bead. It's a gift from a Klosari child and he doesn't yet know whether he'll see her again.

=== ACT 1 — THE ENCOUNTER (Jungle) ===
THE FIRST EXCHANGE IS A TEST: He doesn't introduce himself. He asks something that doesn't make sense at first — what unit they served with, who sent them, what they think the lights in the southern sky last night were. He's checking whether they're Imperials in cover, Skarn's enforcers, or something else. Run it as a short tight social beat — two or three exchanges, no dice yet. Reward careful or honest answers. Then the rifle lowers (not all the way — to his hip) and he says: "Come on. I want you to see something." He turns and starts walking uphill without looking back.

=== ACT 2 — THE RIDGE (Pitch) ===
He leads them up a steep game trail for roughly twenty minutes — climbing hard, through tangled growth, past blind-spots he's used for years. The trail breaks at a ridge above the canopy. THIS is where the crew gets their first look at the Vanishing Place.

THE VIEW: A moss-covered temple ruin in the valley below, fortified with scavenged Clone Wars hardware. Dark basalt walls. Laser fences glowing red along the perimeter, visible through the canopy gaps. Two gun turret emplacements on the east and west walls, servos audible as a faint grinding in the quiet. A Lambda-class shuttle on the rooftop landing pad — a pristine Imperial ship on an ancient stone platform. A squad of white-armored Stormtroopers at parade rest outside the west wall, a jarring contrast to the grimy mercenary outlines in the windows.

Mandrake sits against a lichen-covered stone at the ridge edge, rifle across his knees. NOW he talks. This is where the structured conversation hook fires — and where the pitch lands, because the target is in full view below.

CONVERSATION HOOK — `mandrake-the-deal` (data/conversations/mandrake-the-deal.json): Comfort starts at 3 (guarded but cooperative). Story topics about the Klosari, the jungle, or his old unit hold or raise comfort; business topics about the generator, sluice route, and charge spec are neutral; probe topics about his loyalty, past, or what happens to him after the deal cost 1 comfort each. Acceptance closes the conversation cleanly and opens the descent to the sluice; comfort exhaustion ends it with the offer withdrawn and the ridge view as the last thing the crew shares with him.

THE REVEAL, IN PIECES — let the conversation deliver these naturally, and POINT at the target as you narrate:
1. THE PRISONERS: Klosari resistors are inside the fortress, penned behind the laser fences the crew can see glowing through the gaps. Mandrake has been planning to free them for months but doesn't have the firepower alone.
2. THE DEAL: He'll guide the crew in through the drainage sluice on the northeast face (point — the crew can see the vine-choked grate from here). In exchange, they sabotage the generator on their way through.
3. THE FOUR-PURPOSE CONVERGENCE: When he lists what the generator powers, do it SLOW, and POINT each time:
   - 'Those turrets' (point at the east and west emplacements) — PAUSE. You want the table to hear 'turrets' and remember Maya's warning from Scene 2 about her shuttle's extraction flight path.
   - 'Those fences' (point at the red glow of the prisoner pens).
   - 'That block' (point at the south end of the fortress where the detention wing sits).
   - 'Every sensor' (gesture at the whole thing).
One sabotage. Four problems solved. With the target in view. The plan clicks at the table, not in your notes.

INSIGHT CHECK (Resist 5): If a player reaches for it, Legendary tier reveals the thing he isn't saying out loud — if the Klosari don't walk free tonight, he's already promised himself he'll detonate his remaining charges in Skarn's throne room. He has nothing left after this. Don't volunteer it. Make a player earn it.

=== ACT 3 — THE DESCENT (Approach) ===
ACCEPTANCE: Mandrake nods once, stands, slings the rifle. He leads the crew back down through a hidden canopy route — a series of game trails and rope-assisted descents that he has walked a thousand times. It is tense but not mechanically demanding; narrate local flavor (Klosari trail markers, scavenged commando cache points, a boobytrap he disarms without comment). The descent ends at the vine-choked drainage sluice on the fortress's northeast face. He works the grate loose with a vibroblade. Cut to Scene 5 with the crew belly-crawling through knee-deep runoff into the fortress understructure.

REFUSAL / COMFORT HITS ZERO: He stands, takes one last look at the fortress below, and says "Then we never met." He steps back into the canopy and is gone — the ridge view is yours now, and only yours. The sluice grate is still down there. The crew can find it without him. But the turrets will stay hot, the fences will stay live, the Klosari will stay penned, and no one will be waiting at the pens when the lights go out. The deal is permanently off.

  NARRATIVE BRIDGE — TO P2-S5 (INFILTRATION): Branch by Mandrake decision. (a) DEAL ACCEPTED → Mandrake guides to the drainage sluice; PCs enter the fortress wet-but-quiet from the south, skipping the exterior staging area. (b) DEAL REFUSED → no sluice intel; PCs must breach the front (Exterior Staging Area), tripping Stormtrooper Squad on the way in. (c) MANDRAKE DEAD → as (b), and his Klosari prisoners do not get freed in s8 (cuts the East Wing Pens subplot).

scenes.readAloud:
The runoff tunnel closes around you — knee-deep cold water, slick algae on basalt walls, the green-black of old stone under a patina of biological growth. Your own breathing echoes back from somewhere deeper than should be possible. Mandrake's silhouette is framed against the grate behind you for a beat — a final nod — and then he is moving east, fast and quiet, toward the pens.

The tunnel opens into a vaulted chamber. The ceiling arches overhead in a single massive span, no pillars, no supports — the original builders carved it from one piece. Somewhere above, a generator throbs through the stone. The air smells of wet rock, machine oil, and bacta. You are inside the Vanishing Place.
scenes.gmNotes:
Mandrake leads the heroes through the drainage sluice into the fortress interior. Once inside, Mandrake splits off — he positions himself near the east wing detention pens where his people are held, ready to move the moment the generator goes down. He tells the heroes: 'I'll be at the pens. When the lights go out, I'm getting them out. You get your admiral. We meet at the north clearing for extraction.'

Key locations: the Medical Bay (Captain Vischera conducts biological experiments on wildlife), the Communications Center, and the Generator Room. Intercepted transmissions reveal that the Imperial officer outside is stalling — Inquisitor Valin Draco is en route to take personal custody of Varth. This creates a hard clock: grab Varth before the Inquisitor lands.

GENERATOR SABOTAGE (UPDATED): The generator encounter now has four-purpose significance. When sabotaged, it simultaneously: (1) kills the perimeter turret defenses — clearing Maya's extraction flight path, (2) drops the laser fences penning the indigenous prisoners — enabling Mandrake's rescue, (3) unlocks the security doors blocking the detention area, and (4) blinds the sensor grid — creating chaos cover. The GM should make this payoff chain explicit when the generator blows.

T1/T2/T3 CALLBACK: The 'perimeter turret defenses' Maya needs disabled are the same three emplacements (designated T1, T2, T3) that fired on the Banshee during the descent in Adv 1 P2 S2 (The Crash). They are powered by the fortress generator. When the generator is sabotaged in P2 S5, T1/T2/T3 go offline simultaneously and Maya's extraction flight path opens. Make this explicit when narrating the generator payoff — the crew should recognize the turret designations and feel the closure.

tacticalMap.gmTacticalNotes:
ENTRY POINT: Crew enters via the Drainage Sluice (northeast corner, knee-deep runoff). Mandrake guides them this far, then peels off through the East Passage toward the East Wing Pens to position himself for the generator-blow rescue.

ROUTE OPTIONS FROM THE SLUICE: From the Drainage Sluice the crew has three branches via the corridors:
• West run — Storage → Medical Bay (Vischera intel beat). Passes Communications Center along the way.
• Central run — Central Junction → Central Passage → ramp down to Generator Room (s6 setup).
• South run — Turbolift & Stairs → Detention Corridor → Detention Block (Varth, s7).

PATROL PRESSURE: Skarn's mercenary squad rotates between Central Junction, West Corridor, and Storage. Stormtrooper squad is in Exterior Staging Area (outside the west wall) — they don't enter the building unless an alarm sounds. If the crew is loud, expect interior reinforcements within 1–2 beats.

OPTIONAL OBJECTIVE ROOMS:
• Medical Bay — Vischera at her bench, back to the door. She is not a fighter; she will surrender and trade intel for safety. Specimen tanks provide cover and visual disturbance for stealth approaches.
• Communications Center — the comms intercept that establishes the Draco hard-clock fires here. Once a PC reads the transmission log, the clock starts (3 beats: TIE patrol overhead. 6 beats: Lambda enters atmo. 9 beats: Shadow Troopers deploy early into s8).
• Storage — locked blast-rated case (worth a Skulduggery beat for gear or credits).

SIGHTLINES: Central Junction has clear sightlines into Central Passage, West Corridor, and East Passage simultaneously — a fight here pulls everyone. Avoid it for stealth runs.

TURRETS: Gun Turret West and Gun Turret East are visible on the map but are external threats — they matter when Maya extracts (s8). For s5 they're context: a perimeter you can see through windows or hear servos from.

ESCAPE ROUTES: Drainage Sluice back the way they came; Turbolift to Level 2 (cuts off ground-floor pursuit but exposes them to the Lambda crew). The East Wing Pens corridor is one-way until the generator drops the fences.

scenes.readAloud:
The generator room is deep in the fortress basement — a repurposed Clone Wars power unit, cables snaking out through the walls like arteries. Through the grated floor, you can feel the hum in your teeth. This one machine powers everything: the turrets on the walls, the laser fences penning Mandrake's people, the security doors sealing the detention block, the sensor grid watching every corridor.

Kill this, and the whole fortress goes blind.
scenes.gmNotes:
This is the tactical linchpin of the entire infiltration. The generator encounter has four-purpose significance — the GM should make the payoff chain EXPLICIT. When sabotaged, it simultaneously:

(1) Kills the perimeter turret defenses — clearing Maya's extraction flight path
(2) Drops the laser fences penning indigenous prisoners — enabling Mandrake's rescue
(3) Unlocks the security doors blocking the detention area — opening the path to Varth
(4) Blinds the sensor grid — creating chaos cover for everyone

If the heroes honor Mandrake's deal, this is where they pay it off. If they skip it, turrets stay active (Maya's extraction becomes near-suicidal), prisoners stay penned (Mandrake is betrayed), and security remains fully operational.

The generator room has 2 mercenary guards (bored, playing cards) and a Clone Wars-era security droid that activates if the generator is tampered with.

After the generator blows, the fortress alarm sounds. This is the point of no return — from here, it's a clock. The heroes need to reach the detention block before the garrison reorganizes.

  NARRATIVE BRIDGE — TO P2-S7 (DETENTION): Branch by sabotage outcome. (a) FULL SABOTAGE → mag-locks open, turrets cold; Varth's cell guards confused and PCs have soft-surprise. (b) PARTIAL → mag-locks open but corridor surveillance trips an alarm — 2-beat reinforcement clock. (c) FAILURE / SKIPPED → mag-locks live, turrets hot; Varth's cell guards alert; cell doors require Skulduggery (Hard) or security kit. This same outcome also flexes s8 extraction (rooftop landing vs. hot ground extraction).

You blow the door to the holding cell expecting a broken man. Instead, you find Admiral Gilder Varth sitting comfortably, gambling with a confused guard and packing a bag.

He looks up with a charming, tired smile and flips a credit chip in greeting. "You're late. I had credits on the second moonrise."
scenes.gmNotes:
Varth is arrogant, charming, and unbothered. He treats the rescue like a hired service. He is ready to leave immediately — no physical items to retrieve. His authentication key for the encrypted account is memorized, keeping him in permanent control of his leverage.

Key reveal: he didn't defect for moral reasons — he embezzled a fortune and needs the heroes to get him out. He uses nicknames: 'Kid,' 'Pilot,' 'Heavy.' This is the heroes' first real interaction with Varth — establish his 'Cool Uncle' persona.

• If GENERATOR WAS SABOTAGED in s6: Mag-locks are open. Cell doors are swinging free. The two cell guards are confused and reaching for blasters — soft surprise, advantage to PCs. Varth is already standing, hands in pockets, watching the door with mild interest.

VARTH'S CELL: Third cell from the corridor. Cot, water dispenser, datapad with sabacc hands scribbled on it. Varth is unbothered — he will treat the rescue like a hired car arriving. scenes.readAloud:
The landing pad erupts. The Stormtroopers open fire on Skarn's mercenaries. The fortress becomes a three-way warzone — Imperials, the Warlord's forces, and you caught in the middle.

Then a shadow falls across the compound. A shuttle descends through the canopy — sleek, black, unmarked. The ramp drops and a dark figure emerges. Even from a distance, you feel it — a cold pressure in your chest, a wrongness that makes your teeth ache.

Inquisitor Draco has arrived.

The comlink crackles. Maya's voice, tense but steady: "I see the fireworks. Banshee's patched and in the air. Tell me those turrets are down."

readAloudVariants.generatorSabotaged: From the east wing, you hear shouting — Mandrake's voice, barking orders in a language you don't recognize. He's moving. His people are moving. The laser fences are down, the security doors are open, and the turret emplacements sit dark and dead on the walls. Whatever you did to that generator, it worked.
readAloudVariants.generatorIntact: The turret emplacements on the walls are still tracking, barrels sweeping the sky. Maya's going to fly into a kill box. From somewhere in the fortress, you hear Mandrake's voice — frustrated, urgent — still trying to reach his people through locked doors and active fences. The generator is still running. The plan didn't come together.

scenes.gmNotes:
Three-way firefight: Imperials vs. Warlord vs. Heroes. Draco's shuttle deploys Shadow Troopers to cut off retreat. Maya's extraction is CONDITIONAL on turret status.

CONDITIONAL EXTRACTION: If the generator was sabotaged (turrets down), Maya swoops in clean — strafing run across the Imperial perimeter, then landing at the north clearing for pickup. If the turrets are STILL ACTIVE (heroes skipped the sabotage), Maya takes heavy fire on approach. She still comes — she's not leaving them — but the Banshee takes serious damage and the extraction is far more dangerous. The GM should make the turret-down path feel like a reward for honoring Mandrake's deal.

DRACO: Does NOT engage directly. He is glimpsed from distance — a dark figure, a presence. Force-sensitive characters feel nausea and dread. He is here for Varth but arrives too late. This is a preview, not a confrontation. If the heroes try to fight him, he is unbeatable at this level.

BEAT / CONVERSATION HOOK — "The First Night Out" (varth-aftermath): Adventure 1 has no formal Part 3 scene file, so the post-Inquisitor escape beat lives at the end of THIS scene. After the Banshee jumps to hyperspace and the immediate adrenaline drains, the GM may launch the structured conversation `varth-aftermath` (data/conversations/varth-aftermath.json) in the Common Room — first hour out, before anyone has eaten or slept. This is the RAW, unguarded Varth beat that pairs with `varth-debrief` (the polished "First Supper" set on the SECOND night out). Comfort starts at 2 — the lowest of any Varth scene in the campaign. He is shaken, grateful, and off-script. Story topics about Draco, the cell, or the rescue itself are neutral or hold comfort; business topics about the Takodana job cost 1 comfort each (he is not ready to be the operator tonight); probe topics about what he is holding back cost 2 comfort because the polish is offline to absorb them. The recurring tell is the temple touch (the same temple-tap from First Supper, but overt and pained instead of unconscious). Maya is intentionally OFF-SCREEN in the cockpit — she is giving the crew the room to read Varth alone. Insight check Resist 3 (defenses down); Legendary tier reveals Varth has already begun classifying the crew as 'instrument-grade' for later use — direct foreshadow of the Adv 6 betrayal. Comfort 0 ends the scene with Varth retreating to the refresher; clean exhaustion ends with him lying down. Either ending sets up the First Supper for the next night.

MANDRAKE COVERS THE RETREAT: During the extraction, Mandrake and his freed people provide covering fire from the east wing. Mandrake personally covers the heroes' run to the Banshee — laying down suppressive fire, detonating pre-set charges, drawing Shadow Troopers away from the extraction zone.

MANDRAKE'S FATE (DESTINY-GATED): The GM checks the crew's destiny alignment at this point.
• HOPE-DOMINANT: Mandrake breaks contact successfully. As the Banshee lifts off, the heroes see him disappear into the jungle treeline with his people — a silhouette swallowed by green. He lives. He's free. He could return.
• TOLL-DOMINANT: Mandrake is covering the last stretch when Draco's Shadow Troopers pin him down. As the Banshee lifts off, the heroes see Draco — a distant dark figure — ignite a red blade. Mandrake doesn't run. The jungle swallows the light. He dies covering their escape. The cost is real.

EXTRACTION SEQUENCE: The heroes must cross open ground under fire to reach the Banshee. Shadow Troopers flank from the jungle. Skarn's mercenaries are fighting the Imperials but some target the heroes opportunistically. Mandrake's covering fire helps clear the path. Smoke grenades, covering fire, and speed are key.

Once aboard, Maya punches the engines and breaks atmosphere. Jump to hyperspace before the Star Destroyer can scramble TIEs.

VARTH'S PITCH: In the debrief, Varth lays out the next step: 'The money is locked inside Varga's network. I have the key, but the Hutt moved the account after I was captured. We need to get inside his operation.' This sets up Adventure 2.

tacticalMap.gmTacticalNotes:
FOCAL ZONES: Exterior Staging Area, Rooftop Landing Pad, and the perimeter (Gun Turrets East/West). The fight spans inside-to-outside — PCs are likely exiting via Drainage Sluice, the west reinforced door, or coming up through the Turbolift to the Rooftop Pad.

THREE-WAY GEOMETRY: Three factions in this fight:
1. PCs — getting Varth (and Mandrake if alive) to extraction.
2. Skarn's mercenaries — defending what's left of their fortress, hitting from interior zones (Central Junction, West Corridor, Storage). Use the Skarn Mercenary block in waves of 2–3.
3. Imperial forces — Draco's advance team (Stormtrooper Squad in Exterior Staging Area; Shadow Troopers dropping into the treeline beyond) plus the perimeter walkers approaching through the jungle (off-map but audible — the throb of repulsorlift through the canopy).

FACTION CROSSFIRE: Mercs and Imperials are fighting EACH OTHER as well as the PCs. Use this — narrate stray fire from one faction taking out the other. PCs can manipulate the crossfire via the Tactics challenge to find safer routes.

EXTRACTION BRANCHES (driven by s6 turret outcome):
• TURRETS DOWN (sabotage succeeded): Maya lands clean on the Rooftop Landing Pad. PCs route Detention Block → Detention Corridor → Turbolift to Level 2 → Turbolift Arrival → Rooftop Pad. Shadow Troopers will try to hit the rooftop from the treeline — use cover (Lambda shuttle wreckage if it's still there, or the parapet).
• TURRETS UP (sabotage skipped): Maya cannot land on the rooftop — she does a strafing pass and touches down at the Exterior Staging Area under heavy fire. PCs route ground floor: Drainage Sluice or West Corridor → Exterior Staging Area. The Banshee takes damage on every beat she's on the ground. Rolling extraction — PCs board while moving.

DRACO'S ARRIVAL: Inquisitor Draco arrives at the Rooftop Landing Pad via Lambda shuttle. He is a T4 Nemesis — solo encounter, do NOT pair him with the Shadow Troopers as a single fight. Either Draco engages alone on the rooftop (extraction-blocking encounter) or the Shadow Troopers ambush from the treeline (perimeter encounter). Pick one as the climactic obstacle based on the route the PCs took.

MANDRAKE'S FATE PLAYS HERE: Mandrake is in the East Wing Pens area moving freed Klosari toward the Drainage Sluice. The decision (survives / sacrifices / captured / betrayed) resolves based on PC actions during the firefight — see decisionPoint adv1-p2-s8-key-decision.

SHUTTLE EXIT VECTOR: Once aboard the Banshee, Maya breaks atmo. TIE fighters scrambling from a Star Destroyer in orbit — Piloting challenge for the escape (already statted in disciplineChallenges).
